note: Every entry here describes code that actually runs in this repo. 'kind' states what it is; metrics are empty until an evaluation run produces them. Nothing in this file is aspirational.

models.name: spectral-threshold-vqa
models.description: Excess-green / blue-dominance / brightness thresholds over real pixels. Explainable proxy, not a trained VLM.

models.name: spectral-threshold-grounding
models.description: Keyword-to-landcover-class mask from classical indices. No open-vocabulary grounding model or SAM.

models.name: pixel-difference-change
models.description: Co-registered bi-temporal pixel differencing. Not a learned bi-temporal network.

models.name: speckle-filter-sar-bridge
models.description: Lee/refined-Lee style speckle filtering. Real SAR signal processing, not a translation model.

models.name: threshold-agreement-fusion
models.description: Cross-modal agreement between optical and SAR-backscatter masks. Not a learned fusion model.

models.name: blip-vqa-base
models.dataset: VQAv2 + COCO captions (natural photos, not remote sensing)
models.description: Real pretrained BLIP inference via transformers. Genuine model, genuine weights, genuine forward pass -- but never fine-tuned on satellite/aerial imagery, so its answers on overhead content are out-of-distribution guesses, not measurements. A LoRA fine-tuning script (training/finetune_vqa_lora.py, on RSVQA-LR) exists and specialists/vlm_caption/model.py will load its output via AETHERIS_VLM_LORA_PATH, but no adapter has been trained -- this environment has no GPU or Hugging Face Hub access -- so no RS-adapted checkpoint ships. Optional dependency; absent torch/transformers means this tool is unbound/unavailable rather than silently faked. Every call also returns the actual runtime model_id and lora_applied (whether an adapter really loaded, not just whether a path was configured) alongside the answer, since AETHERIS_VLM_MODEL_ID/AETHERIS_VLM_LORA_PATH can override this static entry per-deployment.

models.name: clipseg-rd64-refined
models.description: Real pretrained CLIPSeg inference via transformers -- genuine open-vocabulary segmentation, but never fine-tuned on satellite/aerial imagery, so masks on overhead content are out-of-distribution guesses. A LoRA fine-tuning script (training/finetune_grounding_lora.py) exists, following the published CLIPSeg-on-FLAIR recipe, and specialists/vlm_grounding/model.py will load its output via AETHERIS_GROUNDING_LORA_PATH, but no adapter has been trained -- this environment has no GPU or Hugging Face Hub access -- so no RS-adapted checkpoint ships. Optional dependency; absent torch/transformers means this tool is unbound/unavailable rather than silently faked. Every call also returns the actual runtime model_id and lora_applied (whether an adapter really loaded, not just whether a path was configured) alongside the mask, since AETHERIS_GROUNDING_LORA_PATH can override this static entry per-deployment.

models.name: clip-vit-base-patch32
models.dataset: WIT (natural photo/caption pairs, not remote sensing)
models.description: Real pretrained CLIP vision-transformer inference via transformers, repurposed for change: cosine distance between corresponding patch embeddings of two acquisitions. A genuine model signal, but not a model trained to detect change, and not fine-tuned on remote sensing -- distances are uncalibrated. Optional dependency; absent torch/transformers means this tool is unbound/unavailable rather than silently faked. Every call also returns the actual runtime model_id alongside the result (no LoRA path for this specialist -- CLIP is used as-is, unadapted).

models.name: embedding-geo-rag
models.description: Sentence-transformer text embeddings over an indexed geospatial corpus, with an in-memory NumPy fallback. Retrieval only — it does not analyse pixels.

models.name: conformal-calibrator
models.description: Split-conformal interval. Ships UNFITTED: with no labelled calibration set it reports method='uncalibrated' and calibrated=false rather than inventing coverage.

models.name: logreg-evidence-fusion
models.description: Logistic-regression fusion over optical pixel-difference, SAR backscatter-difference and temporal-gap evidence channels. Weights are trained via gradient descent (training/fit_fusion_model.py), not hand-set thresholds -- a genuinely learned combiner, unlike pixel-difference-change or threshold-agreement-fusion above. Ships unfitted (informative-prior weights, fusion_model_fitted: false) since no labeled bi-temporal dataset ships with this repo; point AETHERIS_FUSION_MODEL_PATH at a fitted checkpoint to use a real one. Both evidence channels are co-registered before differencing with the same implausible-shift guard as pixel-difference-change (coregistration_reliable reported per channel). An offline fallback, training/fit_fusion_model_synthetic.py, can fit a real (non-hardcoded) checkpoint on locally generated synthetic pairs when Hugging Face Hub access isn't available -- see docs/STATUS.md for why that's a sanity-check fit, not a real-world accuracy claim.

models.name: jev-decision-engine
models.description: JEV (Judgement-Evaluation-Verification) engine — a fast, typed, probabilistic decision engine modelled on the TypeSafe AI System One architecture. Replaces LLM-based routing with zero-token, sub-millisecond decisions using sigmoid/softmax over hand-tuned log-odds feature weights. Handles tool-chain routing (which specialists to invoke), evidence quality scoring, claim-consistency verification, phenomenon classification, and policy/safety guardrails. Saves ~1200 tokens per query for planning alone. All decisions are deterministic and reproducible given the same input state — no randomness, no LLM calls, no network. Weights are informative priors (not learned from data), encoding the same domain knowledge as the rule-based fallback planner but producing calibrated probabilities instead of hard if/else switches.
